snippet.title: Can Exercise Reverse Aging? HIIT, Coffee & Brain Science Tested | Myth or Science (2/6)
snippet.description:
Can science really help us become fitter, younger, smarter and maybe even more perfect?

In this episode of Myth or Science, Dr Jennifer Gardy puts some of the biggest health and human-performance claims to the test. Can exercise reverse aging? Is a few minutes of high-intensity training really as good as a long workout? Can you be fat and fit? Is willpower something you can train like a muscle? And could coffee, cooked food, music, or even sleep change the way our bodies and brains work?

From intense lab tests and skin biopsies to MRI scans, DNA analysis, brain challenges, and music therapy after stroke, Jenn dives into the science behind the myths we hear every day. Along the way, she discovers that some “too good to be true” claims are surprisingly real, while others need a little more nuance.

snippet.title: The Norway Cup: The world's largest football tournament for children (Full Documentary, 2021)
snippet.description:
KIDS CUP is a feel-good family film about the world's largest sports tournament for kids, Norway Cup, in Oslo Norway. We dive into five teenagers from different parts of the world, competing to win the gold medal. They all share the same dream, but they meet unexpected obstacles; unfair referees, homesickness, missing the penalty shot. Thankfully there are girls to flirt with and fun fairs and candy shops to take your mind off your loss. A film about friendship and ambitions.

snippet.title: He Bought Queensland's Worst Paddock
snippet.description:
A Queensland farmer bought a property many would walk away from — paddocks dominated by Giant Rat's Tail Grass. Instead of reaching for herbicides, he's using grazing management, chickens, cover crops and soil health to drive pasture succession and rebuild productivity.

Can livestock, biology and better management outperform chemical weed control? This farm is putting that idea to the test.

In this episode of Farm Learning with Tim Thompson, we visit Belvadier Farm in southern Queensland to see how Nick is tackling one of Australia's most persistent pasture weeds while building a profitable direct-to-consumer farming business.

You'll learn:

• What Giant Rat's Tail Grass is and why it spreads
• The limitations of traditional chemical control methods
• How high-density grazing is creating opportunities for pasture succession
• The role chickens play in fertility management and weed suppression
• How multi-species cover crops are being used to increase diversity
• Why soil health and management decisions influence pasture composition
• Lessons from repairing damaged paddocks and rebuilding resilience

Whether you're managing grazing land, improving pasture productivity, controlling weeds, or exploring regenerative agriculture, this video offers practical insights from a working commercial farm.

snippet.title: Gene Editing Humans: CRISPR, Longevity and the Future of Evolution | Gods Like Us (3/3)
snippet.description:
Lena comes from a family with hereditary deafness. As she thinks about having more children, a controversial scientist offers her a radical possibility: genetically modifying her embryos so her future children could be born with the ability to hear.

But what sounds like a medical breakthrough soon becomes a deeply personal and ethical dilemma. As the scientist pushes Lena to take part in his experiment, she begins to question whether deafness should be treated as a disease at all - and who gets to decide what kind of life is worth “correcting.”

Episode 3 explores one of the most controversial frontiers of modern medicine: genetic modification in human embryos. As science moves closer to designing future generations, this documentary asks how far we should go in the pursuit of health, happiness, and human perfection.

Could gene editing prevent suffering, or are we opening the door to a future where difference is no longer accepted?

snippet.title: How to Convert a Sprayer for Biological Farming
snippet.description:
Can you spray biologicals without buying an expensive purpose-built machine? In this video, Graeme from Biolink shows how an old herbicide sprayer was converted into a dedicated biological spraying unit for less than $10,000.

We take a detailed look inside a modified 800-litre sprayer, covering the pump, plumbing, mixing system, safety upgrades, flood jet selection, and practical changes that make biological applications more accessible for everyday farmers.

Whether you're applying compost extracts, biological fertilisers, fish hydrolysate, blood and bone products, or other regenerative agriculture inputs, this walkthrough demonstrates how existing equipment can often be adapted rather than replaced.

You'll learn:
• How a hydraulic-driven pump improves mixing performance
• Why large-volume plumbing matters for biological products
• How to reduce blockages when spraying organic inputs
• Safety advantages over traditional PTO-driven systems
• How farmers can build a biological sprayer without spending a fortune

This video is ideal for farmers, graziers, regenerative agriculture practitioners, broadacre operators, horticultural producers, and anyone interested in practical biological farming systems.

snippet.title: Gossip, fighting and grief in Singapore's all-female prison | Inside The Women's Prison (2/3)
snippet.description:
In Singapore’s only women’s prison, about 800 inmates eat, sleep and live together in close confines. But when personalities clash and opinions differ, conflicts are bound to arise. 
In the second episode of this three-part series, we witness how rumours spread “faster than Wi-Fi", causing disputes among inmates. With the help of her cellmates, Joanna tries to avoid self-harming. Separately, Halen has to try to control her temper to avoid getting a report from the officers. 

We track peer supporter Christeen as she manages the cell-life with her younger inmates and Haziqah as she tries to pull through a break-up with her fiancé while incarcerated. 

-------

Chapters
▷ 00:00 - In the previous episode
▷ 01:08 - Teo Halen talks about her history of drug addiction 
▷ 06:47 - Christeen prepares a treat for her cellmates
▷ 09:44 - Nur Haziqah has a televisit with her fiancé who is also in prison
▷ 15:03 - Christeen talks about the difficult side of working as a peer supporter
▷ 17:17 - Koh Yu Xin is preparing for her release
▷ 23:00 - Nur Haziqah shares the difficult circumstances that led her to relapse 
▷ 25:46 - Nur Joanna is punished and gets only one hour out of her cell each day
▷ 31:31 - A fight breaks out during outdoor time
▷ 34:28 - Nur Haziqah receive a harsh letter from her fiancé
▷ 36:04 - Every few months, the inmates have to get used to new cellmates
▷ 42:58 - Juliana has a televisit with her daughter
▷ 45:26 - In the next episode

-------

Subscribe to wocomoDOCS: https://goo.gl/sBmGkp
Follow us on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/wocomo 
-------

Women make up about 10% of Singapore’s prison population. And inside the walls of Institution A4, at the Changi Prison Complex, are about 800 female inmates, incarcerated for various offences.  
But as different as they and their offences may be, they all have one thing in common – drugs. Majority of the female inmates at Changi have used and abused drugs or committed crimes related to drugs.  

In this new series, our cameras take us inside the nation’s only women’s prison to see what life is like for a group of diverse inmates. We also meet the all-female team of prison officers watching over them and witness the relationships they build in that world behind bars.

snippet.title: Fencing Wire: How Quality Wire Is Made
snippet.description:
Good fencing wire is not just about price — it is about tensile strength, galvanising, knots, handling, and choosing the right product for the job.

In this factory tour, we look at how stiff stay and hinge joint fencing wire are made, and what farmers should understand before building a fence.

Tim visits the Murray factory in Albury, New South Wales, to see how Australian-made farm fencing wire is manufactured. Matt explains the difference between older hinge joint machines and modern stiff stay wire machines, including why newer machines allow more flexible line wire spacing, picket spacing, knot types, and fence configurations.

This video is useful for farmers, contractors, landholders, fencing suppliers, and anyone choosing prefabricated mesh, stiff stay fencing, hinge joint wire, exclusion fencing, stock fencing, or rural boundary fencing. It explains why carbon content affects tensile strength, why galvanising matters for corrosion resistance, why wire can break if it is nicked or damaged, and why the right wire choice depends on livestock behaviour, terrain, and the purpose of the fence.

If you have ever wondered why one roll of fencing wire costs more than another, why some wire is easier to strain, why heavily galvanised wire matters, or why modern stiff stay products offer more options than older ring lock and hinge joint designs, this factory floor walkthrough gives a practical look behind the product.

This video covers farm fencing wire, stiff stay wire, hinge joint fencing, prefabricated mesh, high tensile wire, soft wire, galvanised fencing wire, stock fencing, exclusion fencing, picket spacing, line wire spacing, wire knots, farm fence construction, wire handling, and real-world fencing decisions for Australian farms and rural properties.

snippet.title: No-Till Cropping: Compost, Discs and Lower Inputs
snippet.description:
No-till cropping, compost extract and biological seed dressing are helping Chris Smith lower input pressure on a 2,400-acre farm at Natimuk, Victoria.
Chris shows the mix, the compost system and the Ryan NT disc setup behind a more resilient cropping program.

At Grass Flat near Natimuk, Chris Smith is working through the same problems many cropping farmers are facing: rising fertiliser costs, chemical handling risk, residue management, fuel use and the pressure to keep producing reliable crops in a difficult season.

In this Farm Learning episode, Chris takes us through the practical changes he has made on his cropping and grazing farm, including on-farm composting, compost extract, biological seed dressing, seed inoculation, and the move to Ryan NT discs on a 10 m seeding bar.

Chris shows how he makes a 20 L biological seed dressing using worm extract, kelp, humates, molasses and compost extract, and explains how that mix is used across four tonnes of seed. He also talks through the seed treatments and chemical inputs he has removed from his routine, why chemical handling was a concern, and how he is trying to build more biological resilience into the cropping system.

The video also looks at his composting system, including coffee grounds, duck manure, bedding, hay, wood chips, covered compost rows, moisture management, fungal activity and the use of compost as a biological fertiliser source.

Later in the episode, Chris explains why he moved from knife points toward Ryan NT discs, how the disc setup helps handle residue, why the tractor works less hard, and how he can cover more hectares in a day while reducing fuel pressure.

This video is useful for farmers, croppers, contractors, landholders and anyone interested in practical no-till cropping, biological farming, compost extract, seed inoculation, direct drill seeding, disc seeding, soil biology, residue handling, lower chemical inputs and real-world regenerative agriculture in Australian dryland farming systems.
